description:
v1.1.1 maintenance pass. Strictly scoped. Two sub-items, in this order:

A. Replay keybind — UI exposure (Issue #2). The data layer is already wired: src/store.ts defines HotkeyBindings { toggle, gif, replay } with default replay = "F8", persists it under KEY_HOTKEY_BINDINGS, and the renderer pushes it to main via window.cove.setHotkeyBindings. electron/main.ts already registers replay via globalShortcut and routes "cove:hotkey" → action "replay". App.tsx already handles the replay action. The ONLY gap is that src/components/HotkeysDialog.tsx SLOTS array does not include a row for the replay slot, so users can't rebind it from the existing Customize Hotkeys dialog. Fix = add a replay row to SLOTS with an appropriate label/hint. No store changes, no main changes, no IPC changes, no new dialog.

B. Replay/crop timer state — UI-state-level investigation and minimum fix (Issue #4). Touch only src/App.tsx and src/store.ts timer-related state (startedAt, elapsedMs, tickElapsed, resetElapsed) and the interval at App.tsx line ~126. Acceptable fixes: ensure elapsed resets to 0 at the right transitions, ensure the interval does not double-tick or leak across replay save / crop cancel, ensure the timer does not run during preparing/finalizing/replay-buffer-only states. If a fix is not obviously UI-state-level, STOP and document the finding in the handover instead of patching. Do not change MediaRecorder, ffmpeg, recorder.ts, recorder-client.ts, or any capture/encoder logic.

Acceptance criteria:
1. Replay slot appears in the Customize Hotkeys dialog alongside Toggle and GIF, with the same rebind UX (click → press keys → save).
2. Saving a new replay binding persists across app restart (verifies via existing writeHotkeyBindings → KEY_HOTKEY_BINDINGS path).
3. Saving a new replay binding registers the new accelerator with Electron globalShortcut on the next applyHotkeys() pass (verifies via existing setHotkeyBindings IPC flow); the old binding is released.
4. Reset button in the Customize Hotkeys dialog restores replay to the F8 default.
5. Pressing the configured replay key triggers the existing replay save flow exactly as F8 does today.
6. Timer behavior: at minimum, no regression vs v1.1.0. If a UI-state-only timer bug is found and fixed, document the exact symptom and the exact diff in the handover.

Files in scope (read/write):
- src/components/HotkeysDialog.tsx (add replay SLOT entry)
- src/App.tsx (timer interval/effect only, if a UI-state fix is warranted)
- src/store.ts (timer state shape only, if a UI-state fix is warranted; HotkeyBindings already includes replay — do not modify)
- RELEASES.md (only if release is later requested)

Files explicitly out of scope:
- electron/main.ts (hotkey wiring already works; do not touch)
- electron/recorder.ts, electron/ffmpeg.ts (capture/encoder)
- src/recorder-client.ts (capture)
- electron/preload.ts (IPC surface already exposes hotkey + setHotkeyBindings)

Out of scope for this ticket:
- Any MediaRecorder rework.
- Any change to capture pipeline, encoder selection, hardware encoder paths, ffmpeg invocation, or audio sidecar logic.
- Issue #1 (crop area selection) and Issue #3 (source-not-recording-until-hovered). Both are folded into v2 design tickets.
- Any UI redesign beyond adding one row to the existing hotkeys dialog.
- Any new settings, new preferences surface, or new IPC channels.

Verification:
- npm typecheck (or repo-equivalent — check package.json scripts before assuming).
- Manual: open Customize Hotkeys, rebind replay to a non-default combo, save, restart app, verify persistence, verify new accelerator fires replay action and old one does not.
- Manual: start/stop a normal recording and observe timer starts at 0, counts up, returns to 0 on stop.
- Manual: with replay buffer running but no active recording, verify the recording timer does not advance (replay buffer is separate from elapsed).
- git status --short and a summary of changed files.

Release rules (only if user later asks to ship):
- Per global rule, every shipped artifact must have a .sha256 sidecar.
- Per RELEASES.md, use only release/build/package instructions defined inside this repo. Do not borrow patterns from sibling projects.
- Do not build, package, tag, or publish without explicit user request.

Failure-reset rule: if the same timer-state issue survives two fix attempts in implementation, stop and hand back per WORKFLOW.md "Failed fix reset" — do not keep patching speculatively.
title: Optional v1.1.1 maintenance: replay keybind + timer state cleanup
